paper.title: KL-UCB-switch: optimal regret bounds for stochastic bandits from both a distribution-dependent and a distribution-free viewpoints

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed stochastic bandit over [0,1] (known horizon T)
unmapped: model is the non-parametric class of all distributions over [0,1]
settings.definition_quote: We consider the simplest case of a bounded stochastic bandit problem with finitely many arms indexed by $a \in \{1,\ldots,K\}$ and with rewards in~$[0,1]$. ... each arm $a$ is associated with an unknown probability distribution $\nu_a \in \pset$.

settings.name_in_paper: K-armed stochastic bandit over [0,1] (anytime, unknown horizon)
unmapped: model is the non-parametric class of all distributions over [0,1]
settings.definition_quote: We consider the simplest case of a bounded stochastic bandit problem with finitely many arms ... with rewards in~$[0,1]$. ... A standard doubling trick fails ... This is why a dedicated anytime version of our algorithm is needed.

source.label: th:distribfree
source.quote: Given $T \geq 1$, the regret of the KL-UCB-Switch algorithm, tuned with the knowledge of $T$ and the switch function $f(T, K) = \lfloor (T/K)^{1/5} \rfloor$, is uniformly bounded over all bandit problems $\unu$ over $[0,1]$ by R_T \leq (K-1) + 23 \sqrt{KT}.

results.notes: Regret defined via means (sum Delta_a E[N_a(T)]), so pseudo-regret.

symbols.C_a: O_T(1) remainder term depending on the instance and K but bounded in T (closed form in eq. detailedboundTh3)

source.label: th:distribdependentloglog
source.quote: Given $T \geq 1$, the KL-UCB-Switch algorithm, tuned with the knowledge of $T$ and the switch function $f(T, K) = \lfloor (T/K)^{1/5} \rfloor$, ensures that for all bandit problems $\unu$ over $[0,1]$ with $\mu^\star \in (0,1)$, for all sub-optimal arms~$a$, for all $T \geq K/\min\big\{1-\mu^\star, \,(\Delta_a/9)^{12}\big\}$, \E[N_a(T)] \leq \frac{\ln T - \ln \ln T}{\Kinf(\nu_a, \mu^\star)} + \O_T(1)

results.notes: Bound on expected number of pulls of a sub-optimal arm (per-arm), not regret directly; regret follows by summing Delta_a E[N_a(T)]. O_T(1) term recorded via symbol C_a.

tuning: augmented exploration function phi(x) = ln_+(x(1+ln_+^2 x))

source.label: th:distfreeanytime
source.quote: The regret of the anytime version of KL-UCB-Switch algorithm above, tuned with the switch function $f(t, K) = \lfloor (t/K)^{1/5} \rfloor$, is uniformly bounded over all bandit problems $\unu$ over $[0,1]$ as follows: for all $T \geq 1$, R_T \leq (K-1) + 44 \sqrt{KT}.

symbols.C_a: instance-dependent constant (the O_T((ln T)^{6/7}) remainder divided by (ln T)^{6/7}, bounded as T grows)

tuning: augmented exploration function phi(x) = ln_+(x(1+ln_+^2 x))

source.label: th:asymptoticanytime
source.quote: The anytime version of KL-UCB-Switch algorithm above, tuned with the switch function $f(t, K) = \lfloor (t/K)^{1/5} \rfloor$, ensures that for all bandit problems $\unu$ over $[0,1]$, for all sub-optimal arms $a$, for all $T \geq 1$, \E[N_a(T)] \leq \frac{\ln T }{\Kinf(\nu_a, \mu^\star)} + \O_T\bigl( (\ln T)^{6/7} \bigr)

results.notes: Per-arm pull-count bound. Implies asymptotic optimality limsup E[N_a]/ln T <= 1/Kinf.

source.label: prop:MOSS
source.quote: For a known horizon $T \geq 1$, for all bandit problems $\unu$ over $[0,1]$, MOSS achieves a regret bound smaller than $R_T \leq (K-1) + 17 \sqrt{KT}$.

results.notes: Re-derivation of known MOSS result (Audibert & Bubeck 2009) with the paper's own constant; paper claims no improvement on the result itself.

source.label: prop:MOSS-adaptive
source.quote: For all horizons $T \geq 1$, for all bandit problems $\unu$ over $[0,1]$, MOSS-anytime achieves a regret bound smaller than $R_T \leq (K-1) + c \sqrt{KT}$ where $c = 30$ for $\varphi = \ln_+$ and $c = 33$ for the augmented exploration function

results.notes: Re-derivation of anytime MOSS result (Degenne & Perchet 2016).

source.label: prop:MOSS-adaptive
source.quote: For all horizons $T \geq 1$, for all bandit problems $\unu$ over $[0,1]$, MOSS-anytime achieves a regret bound smaller than $R_T \leq (K-1) + c \sqrt{KT}$ where $c = 30$ for $\varphi = \ln_+$ and $c = 33$ for the augmented exploration function $\varphi(x) = \log_+\!\big(x  (1 + \log_+^2 x)\big)$
